title: Welcome to NoteLiner
body:
# Welcome to NoteLiner

NoteLiner is an outliner-style Markdown note-taking app. A project is a
folder: your notes are plain `.md` files in it, in sub-folders if you want
them, and nothing else is needed to read them.

## What's in this Help

- Toolbar buttons: every icon on the left toolbar has a page describing
  what it does and which keyboard shortcut triggers it.
- Panels: the Files, Outline, Tags, Search, Backlinks, Attachments, and
  Log panels each have their own page.
- Workflow guides: how to create files and folders, start notes from
  templates, import documents, link notes with `[[wikilinks]]`, and export
  to HTML, PDF, or Markdown.

## Tips for using this window

- Type into the search box on the left to find pages whose content
  contains your term. The other pages are greyed out.
- Help stays open while you work. Move it by its title bar, and resize it
  from its corner.
- Press `F1` or use the close button to close it.

title: Getting Started
body:
# Getting Started

1. Open a folder with the Open Folder toolbar button (or `Ctrl+O`). Any
   folder opens. Its Markdown files become notes, and its sub-folders
   become the folders of the tree. A new project is an empty folder.
2. Create your first note with New Item (`Ctrl+N`) and give it a short,
   descriptive name. The file is named from a slug of the name, such as
   `kickoff-notes.md`, and is selected at once.
3. Write in Markdown. Links, headings, lists, code blocks, and
   `[[wikilinks]]` all render in the Preview pane (`Ctrl+P`).
4. Organize. Make folders with New Item, drag notes into them, apply
   tags from the Tags pane, filter the Files pane by tag, and connect
   notes with `[[wikilinks]]`.

NoteLiner keeps no history of a note's earlier versions and does not sync.
The project is an ordinary folder, so you can back it up, sync it, or keep
it in Git with the tools you already use. See the Folders page.

title: Home
body:
# Home

Closes the open project and returns you to the open screen, where you can
open another folder or pick from your recent projects.

Before closing, NoteLiner saves your window layout (panel widths, visible
panes, open tabs, and open folders) and writes any edit that is waiting to
be saved.

title: Open Folder
body:
# Open Folder

Shortcut: `Ctrl+O`

Opens a system folder picker. Choose any folder on disk and it opens:

- Every `.md` file in it, at any depth, is a note, and every `.mmd` or
  `.mermaid` file is a diagram.
- Every sub-folder is a folder in the Files pane.
- Folders and files whose names start with `.` or `_` are left out, with
  everything in them.
- NoteLiner writes one file of its own, `noteliner.json`, at the top of
  the folder. No note is changed by opening.

To start a new project, make an empty folder and open it.

NoteLiner remembers recently opened folders on the open screen.

title: New Item
body:
# New Item

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+N`

Opens the New Item dialog, which makes a note, a presentation, a diagram,
or a folder. Pick one in the Type row. You are asked for a name and a
folder, and for a note, presentation, or diagram, an optional set of tags.
The folder starts as the selected folder, or the folder of the selected
note. The name you have typed and the folder you have picked are kept when
you change the type.

A note's file is named from a slug of the name, such as `kickoff-notes.md`,
and is selected for editing right away.

With Folder chosen, the new folder is made inside the folder you pick. If
its name can't be used, the dialog says why. See the **Folders** page.

New files can also be created on the fly by clicking a *dangling*
`[[wikilink]]` in the Preview pane — see the **Wikilinks** page.

With Presentation chosen, the dialog shows a Theme list for the slides. It
starts as the NoteLiner theme you are using. See the **Presenting** page.

If the project has any **templates**, the dialog shows a *Template* dropdown
so a new note can start from a saved skeleton instead of a blank body — see
the **Templates** page.

title: Folders
body:
# Folders

The folders in the Files pane are the folders on disk. A folder holds
notes, diagrams, and other folders.

## Making a folder

Choose Folder in the New Item dialog (`Ctrl+N`). The New Folder button in
the Files pane's header, New Folder in the right-click menu of a folder or
of the empty part of the tree, and New Folder in the Command Palette
(`Ctrl+K`) open the same dialog with Folder already chosen. The dialog
starts with the selected folder, or the folder of the selected note, or the
top with nothing selected, and you can pick another in its Folder list.

A folder's name is its name on disk. It can't be empty, start with `.` or
`_`, or contain `/`, `\`, `<`, `>`, `:`, `"`, `|`, `?`, or `*`. Two folders
in one place can't have the same name, ignoring case.

## Moving

Drag a note or a folder onto a folder to move it there, or drop it on the
empty part of the tree to move it to the top. Move... in the right-click
menu lists the folders to choose from.

- Moving a note moves its file, and its attachments with it.
- A note moved into a folder that already has a file of that name gets
  `-2` on its file name. The name you see doesn't change.
- A folder can't move into itself, or to where a folder of its name is.
- There is no drag to reorder. Each folder's notes are in the sort chosen
  in the header.

## Renaming and deleting

Double-click a folder, or press `F2`, to rename it. The notes in it keep
their tags, attachments, and open tabs.

Delete, in the right-click menu or with `Ctrl+D` when a folder is selected,
asks first and says what the folder holds. The folder and everything in it
go to the system's trash. Deleted notes and attachments go to the trash
too.

## Files NoteLiner doesn't show

- Folders and files whose names start with `.` or `_`, with everything in
  them. This covers `.git`, `_attachments`, and `_templates`.
- Files that aren't notes or diagrams, such as PDFs. They are left alone.

## Changes made by other programs

You can add, move, rename, and remove notes and folders with a file
manager, a sync tool, or Git while NoteLiner has the project open.
NoteLiner checks while its window has the focus, and when it regains it.

- New notes and folders appear, and removed ones leave the tree.
- A note moved to another folder keeps its name, tags, and tab.
- A note renamed outside NoteLiner takes its name from the new file name.
- An open note that changed on disk reloads. If it has unsaved edits, a
  dialog offers Reload and Keep Mine.

## Using Git yourself

NoteLiner doesn't run Git. A project that is a Git repository opens as any
folder does, and NoteLiner never reads or changes `.git`. Your edits show
as uncommitted changes, which you commit and push yourself.

title: Templates
body:
# Templates

Templates are reusable note skeletons stored as plain markdown in the
project's `_templates/` folder. They are **not** notes — they never
appear in the file tree, search, or backlinks. They are files in the
project folder, so they are copied and backed up with it.

## Using a template

When a project contains at least one template, the **New Item** dialog
(`Ctrl+N`) shows a *Template* dropdown. Pick one and the new note
starts from that template's body instead of a blank document. Choose *Blank*
for the default behaviour.

## Creating a template

Select a note and run **Save as Template** from the Command Palette
(`Ctrl+K`). The note's current name and editor contents are saved as a
new template. You can then open `_templates/<name>.md` and edit it —
for example to add placeholders.

## Placeholders

When a note is created from a template, these placeholders in the template
body are filled in automatically:

- `{{title}}` — the new note's name (e.g. `Meeting Notes`)
- `{{date}}` — the current date, `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-05-31`)
- `{{time}}` — the current time, `HH:MM` 24-hour (e.g. `14:30`)
- `{{datetime}}` — date and time together (e.g. `2026-05-31 14:30`)

Any other `{{...}}` text is left untouched.

title: Import Document
body:
# Import Document

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+I`

Imports an external document into the current project, converting it to
markdown. Embedded images are extracted into the project's `_attachments/`
folder and rewritten as markdown image references.

A summary line appears in the Log pane noting how many images were
extracted and whether any tables were stripped during conversion.

title: Undo and Redo
body:
# Undo and Redo

Shortcuts: `Ctrl+Z` to undo, `Ctrl+Shift+Z` or `Ctrl+Y` to redo

The Undo and Redo buttons on the left toolbar act on the file in the active
tab: a note, a presentation, or a diagram. A button is off when there is
nothing to undo or to redo. Both are also in the Command Palette.

Every open tab has its own history, and it is kept while you work in other
tabs. The history is held in memory, so it is gone when you quit NoteLiner.
Your text is not: every edit is saved to the file a moment after you make
it, and an undo is saved in the same way.

- Typing without a pause is one step. A paste, a list change, and an edit
  in the Slides pane are each one step.
- In a diagram, a drag is one step, and so is drawing a shape and typing
  its label.
- When another program changes the file, the new content is one step. Undo
  brings back what you had.
- A tag added in the Tags pane and a change in Presentation Settings are
  not steps. Change them back where you made them.
- The keys work while the keyboard is in the editor, on the canvas, or
  nowhere, for example after a click in the Slides pane. In a text field
  of a pane or a dialog, they undo that field's typing.

## Reopen Closed Tab

Shortcut: `Ctrl+Shift+W`

Brings back the tab you closed last, with its history, cursor, and scroll.
NoteLiner keeps the last ten tabs you closed in this project. A file that
was deleted since is skipped.

## Limits

A note keeps up to 1,000 steps and a diagram up to 200, and each keeps at
most 8 MiB. All tabs together keep at most 64 MiB. Past a limit the oldest
steps go first: from closed tabs, then from the tabs you left longest ago.

title: Files Panel
body:
# Files Panel

Shortcut: `Ctrl+E`

Toggles the Files sidebar pane. It shows the project folder as a tree: its
folders first, then its notes and diagrams. Click a note to open it, and
click a folder to open or close it.

The header has a New Folder button, the sort (Name A-Z, Name Z-A, Last
Modified, or Created), and the tag filter. The sort applies to the notes of
each folder. Folders always come first, in name order.

Right-click a note for a menu with quick actions: open its folder in your
system file manager, duplicate (`Ctrl+Shift+D`) or rename it, move it to
another folder, delete it, clear all tags, toggle the preview, or export
the note to HTML, PDF, or Markdown.

Duplicate opens a dialog pre-filled with the source note's tags and a
`<name>-Copy` name, then makes a copy beside the source.

Double-click a note or a folder, or press `F2`, to rename it in place.

Use `Ctrl+PgUp` and `Ctrl+PgDn` to step through the notes without leaving
the keyboard.

See the Folders page for making, moving, and deleting folders.

title: Outline Panel
body:
# Outline Panel

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+O`

Toggles the **Outline** sidebar pane. The Outline shows every heading in
the current note as a tree. Click any heading to jump straight to that
section of the editor.

The outline updates live as you type, so it doubles as a structural
overview while you write.

title: Tags Panel
body:
# Tags Panel

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+T`

Toggles the **Tags** sidebar pane. Lists every tag applied to the
currently selected file.

- **Add a tag:** `Ctrl+T` (or `Ctrl+Shift++` when the Tags pane is
  visible).
- **Remove a tag:** `Ctrl+Y`.

A note's tags are stored in the YAML frontmatter at the top of its file
when frontmatter writing is turned on in Settings. Otherwise they live only
in the project index. You can also type tags into the frontmatter in the
editor. See the Editor page.

title: Attachments Panel
body:
# Attachments Panel

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+A`

Toggles the **Attachments** side panel (right side). It shows the
attachments of the selected note: images, PDFs, and other files pulled in
by imports, pasted, or dropped on the editor. A note's attachments are kept
in `_attachments/` inside the note's own folder, and they move with the
note.

From here you can preview attachments, copy their paths, or insert a
markdown reference into the active note.

title: Search Panel
body:
# Search Panel

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+F`

Toggles the **Search** sidebar pane and focuses the search input.
Performs a project-wide, full-text search across every note. Results group
by file; click any matched line to jump to that location in the editor.

To search *inside* the current file only, use the editor's built-in
find with `Ctrl+Shift+F`.

title: Backlinks Panel
body:
# Backlinks Panel

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+B`

Toggles the **Backlinks** sidebar pane. Lists every other note in the
project that contains a `[[wikilink]]` pointing to the currently
selected file.

Each entry shows the source note's name and the specific line containing
the link. Click an entry to jump straight to that line in the source
note.

title: Log Panel
body:
# Log Panel

Shortcut: `Ctrl+L`

Toggles the Activity Log at the bottom of the window. It shows messages
from NoteLiner: import results, and what an AI assistant did through the
MCP server.

Drag the top edge to resize.

title: Settings
body:
# Settings

Shortcut: `Ctrl+,`

Opens the Settings dialog:

- UI: theme, UI scale, and custom window titlebar.
- Project: the open project's folder, and whether NoteLiner writes YAML
  frontmatter into `.md` files.
- Editor: the editor's font, text size, and line height, and spell checking.
- Diagrams: the grid and dimension lines of the diagram canvas, and the
  font of diagram labels.
- MCP: the local server that lets an AI assistant read and write notes.
- Keyboard Shortcuts: a complete list of every command and its shortcut,
  generated from the command registry, so it always matches what the app
  responds to.

title: About
body:
# About

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+I`

Shows the **About** dialog with the application name, version, and a
link to the GitHub repository.

title: Help
body:
# Help

**Shortcut:** `F1`

Opens this Help window, from the Help button at the bottom of the left
toolbar or with the key. Press `F1` again, or use the window's close
button, to close it.

Help is a window, not a dialog. You can move it, resize it, and keep
working in NoteLiner while it is open, for example with the
**Presentation Formatting** page beside the presentation you are writing.

Type in the search box on the left to filter the index by content. Pages
that do not match are greyed out.

title: Editor
body:
# Editor

The central pane is a plain-text Markdown editor. Everything you type is
saved to the note's file a moment after you stop typing.

## Frontmatter

The editor shows a note's whole file. If the file starts with a `---`
block of YAML frontmatter, the block is shown at the top in a dimmer
colour, and you can edit it.

- `tags` are the note's tags. Change them here or in the Tags pane.
- `created` is the date the note was made.
- `presentation:` holds a deck's settings, as set in Presentation Settings.
- Any other field is yours. NoteLiner keeps it as you typed it.

NoteLiner writes `tags` and `created`, and puts them back if they are
removed. The preview, exports, slides, search, the word count, and the
spell check all leave the block out. While a half-typed line stops the
block from being read, the status bar says "Frontmatter can't be read" and
the note's tags stay as they were.

A note's name is not in its file. Rename a note in the Files pane.

## Useful editor shortcuts

- `Ctrl+B`: bold the selection (wraps it in `**`, or toggles it off)
- `Ctrl+I`: italicize the selection (wraps it in `*`, or toggles it off)
- `Ctrl+Shift+F`: find in current file
- `Ctrl+P`: toggle the Preview pane
- `Alt+.`: insert right arrow (→) at caret
- `Alt+,`: insert left arrow (←) at caret

Headings, lists, code blocks, blockquotes, tables, images, and
`[[wikilinks]]` all render in Preview as you'd expect from standard
Markdown.

title: Preview Pane
body:
# Preview Pane

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+P`

The Preview pane renders the current note's markdown as styled HTML.
`[[wikilinks]]` become clickable: solid links open the target note;
dashed (*dangling*) links offer to create the target note when clicked.

Right-click anywhere inside the preview for a context menu with
**Select All**, **Copy**, and the **Save to HTML / PDF / Markdown**
export actions.

Drag the left edge of the pane to resize it.

title: Wikilinks
body:
# Wikilinks

Type `[[Note Name]]` anywhere in a note to link to another note by
name. In Preview:

- Links that resolve to an existing note are solid and clickable —
  clicking jumps to that note.
- Links that don't resolve appear with a **dashed underline**. Clicking
  one opens the **New Item** dialog pre-filled with that name.

Pipe syntax (`[[Real Name|Display Text]]`) lets you show a different
label while still pointing at the target.

The **Backlinks** panel lists every note pointing *at* the current
note, so you can navigate your link graph in either direction.

title: Export to HTML / PDF / Markdown
body:
# Export

NoteLiner can save the current note as a standalone document outside of
the project folder:

- **Save to HTML** — fully styled HTML.
- **Save to PDF** — a Letter page with half-inch margins.
- **Save to Markdown** — a clean `.md` copy without frontmatter or
  project metadata.

Trigger any of these from:

- the Preview pane's right-click context menu, or
- the Files pane's right-click context menu on the selected file.

After saving, NoteLiner opens your Downloads folder so you can pick up
the exported file.

title: Presenting
body:
# Presenting

A presentation is a note with slides. Make one with Presentation in the
New Item dialog, or with Convert to Presentation... in a note's right-click
menu.

See the **Presentation Formatting** page for how to write slides, notes,
layouts, headers, and footers.

## Themes

A presentation has its own theme, so it looks the same whatever theme
NoteLiner is in. There is one for each NoteLiner theme, in the same colours:
Midnight, Dark, Dark-Purple, Light, Light-Purple, Light-Mulberry, and
Light-Rasberryson.
A slide's title sits on a band of the theme's accent colour. A title
slide has no band, and its heading takes the accent colour, as links do.

- Pick the theme in the New Item dialog when you make the presentation. It
  starts as the NoteLiner theme you are using.
- Change it later in Presentation Settings.
- To give one slide another theme, put a line such as
  `<!-- slide: class="theme-light-mulberry" -->` under its heading.

## Starting

While a presentation is open, the left toolbar shows three more buttons
below Search and Backlinks: Slides, Present, and Present with Speaker View.

| Action | Key | Starts at |
|---|---|---|
| Present | `F5` | The slide the cursor is in |
| Present from the First Slide | `Shift+F5` | Slide 1 |
| Present with Speaker View | `Alt+F5` | The slide the cursor is in |

You can also use:

- Present in the right-click menu of a presentation in the Files pane.
- The play button in the Slides pane's header.
- Present from This Slide in the right-click menu of a slide in the Slides
  pane.
- The Command Palette (`Ctrl+K`).

## While presenting

The presentation fills the screen. Move the mouse to show a small bar with
Previous, Next, the slide number, and Exit. It hides after three seconds.

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| `Right`, `Down`, `Space`, `Page Down`, `Enter`, `N`, or a click | Next slide |
| `Left`, `Up`, `Page Up`, `Backspace`, `P` | Previous slide |
| `Home` / `End` | First / last slide |
| `S` | Show or hide your notes |
| `F11` | Leave or return to full screen, still presenting |
| `D` | Move to the next display (with two or more displays) |
| `Escape` | Stop presenting |

## More than one display

With two or more displays connected, a presentation's right-click menu in
the Files pane lists them (Present on Display 1, Present on Display 2, and
so on), and so does the Command Palette. Picking one presents there, and
NoteLiner remembers it: `F5` uses that display from then on, whenever it is
connected. While presenting, `D` or the display button on the controls
moves to the next display.

Present on This Window's Display in the Command Palette goes back to
presenting on the display the NoteLiner window is on.

## Speaker view

Present with Speaker View opens a second window with the current slide,
the next slide, your notes, a timer, and the clock. Drag it to your own
screen. Where the system allows it (not on Wayland), `X` in it swaps the
two screens.

title: Presentation Formatting
body:
# Presentation Formatting

A presentation is a note with a `presentation:` block in its frontmatter.
Its slides are written in Markdown. This page lists what you can write.
See the **Presenting** page for how to show one.

## Slides

| You write | It does |
|---|---|
| `## Heading` | Starts a new slide, with the heading as its title |
| `---` on a line of its own | Starts a new slide with no title |
| `# Heading` at the top, with one line under it or none | The title slide |

Which headings start a slide is set by "New slide starts at" in
Presentation Settings. With the usual setting, `#` and `##` start a slide
and `###` does not.

A slide's title sits on a band of the theme's accent colour. A title slide,
a quote slide, and a full picture have no band.

## Text

| You write | You get |
|---|---|
| `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~struck~~` | Bold, italic, and struck text |
| `` `code` `` | Code in the text |
| `[text](https://example.com)` | A link |
| `- item` or `1. item` | A list |
| `- [ ]` and `- [x]` | A task list with boxes |
| `> text` | A quote |
| Three backticks above and below | A code block |
| `\| a \| b \|` rows | A table. `:-:` centres a column and `--:` puts it on the right |
| `<mark>text</mark>` | A highlight |
| `<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>` | A key cap |
| `$x^2$` and `$$x^2$$` | Math in the text and on a line of its own |
| `![alt](picture.png)` | A picture |
| A YouTube address, or `![](film.mp4)` | A card with a link to the video |

## Layouts

NoteLiner picks a slide's layout from what is on it.

| On the slide, under the title | Layout | Looks like |
|---|---|---|
| Nothing, or one line with no title | `hero` | Large and centred |
| One block | `title-body` | The title, then the block |
| Two blocks | `split` | Side by side |
| Three or more blocks | `grid` | Two columns |
| Only a quote | `quote` | A large centred quote |
| Only a table | `table` | The table at full width |
| Only a picture, with no title | `full-bleed` | The picture fills the slide |

A block is a paragraph, a list, a quote, a table, a code block, or a
picture. To choose the layout yourself, use `layout=` as shown below.

## Options for one slide

Put a `slide:` comment on the line under the slide's heading:

```
## Our plan
<!-- slide: layout=split bg=#3b2a5c -->
```

| Option | Does |
|---|---|
| `layout=split` | Uses that layout: `hero`, `title-body`, `split`, `grid`, `full-bleed`, `quote`, or `table` |
| `bg=#3b2a5c` | The slide's background colour: a hex colour, `rgb(...)`, or a colour name |
| `class="theme-light"` | Another theme for this slide, such as `theme-midnight` or `theme-light-mulberry` |
| `header="Text"` | This slide's header, in place of the presentation's |
| `footer="Text"` | This slide's footer, in place of the presentation's |
| `notes-only` | Leaves the slide out of the presentation. It stays in the note |

Several options go in one comment, with spaces between them. Put quotes
around a value that has a space in it.

## Speaker notes

```
<!-- notes
Welcome everyone. Start with the story about the launch.
-->
```

Notes belong to the slide they are written in. They show under the slide
in the preview, in the speaker view, and when you press `S` while
presenting. A short note fits on one line: `<!-- notes: Thank the team. -->`

## Header, footer, and slide numbers

Open Presentation Settings and fill in Header or Footer. The text shows on
every slide except a full picture: the header at the top above a thin
line, and the footer at the bottom. "Show slide numbers" puts the slide's
number at the bottom right.

These placeholders are filled in for you:

| Placeholder | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `{{name}}` | The note's name |
| `{{date}}` | Today's date |
| `{{time}}` | The time now |
| `{{page}}` | The slide's number |
| `{{total}}` | The number of slides |

For example, the footer `{{name}} · {{page}} / {{total}}` shows as
"Kickoff · 3 / 12".

## The presentation block

Presentation Settings writes these into the note's frontmatter. You can
also edit them in the editor.

```
---
presentation:
  theme: midnight
  aspect: "16:9"
  slideLevel: 2
  header: ""
  footer: "{{name}} · {{page}} / {{total}}"
  slideNumbers: true
  firstSlideTitle: true
---
```

| Setting | Values |
|---|---|
| `theme` | `midnight`, `dark`, `darkPurple`, `light`, `lightPurple`, `lightMulberry`, or `lightRasberryson` |
| `aspect` | `"16:9"`, `"16:10"`, or `"4:3"` |
| `slideLevel` | `0` for only `---`, `1` for `#`, `2` for `#` and `##`, `3` to add `###` |
| `header`, `footer` | Text, with the placeholders above |
| `slideNumbers` | `true` or `false` |
| `firstSlideTitle` | `true` styles a leading `#` heading as the title slide |

title: Command Palette
body:
# Command Palette

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+K` (also `Ctrl+Shift+P`)

Opens the Command Palette — a fuzzy-searchable list of every action in
the app. Type a few letters of any command name to find it; `Enter`
runs it.

Recently used commands appear at the top of the list, so frequent
actions stay one keystroke away.

title: Toolbar Toggle
body:
# Toolbar Toggle

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+E`

Hides or shows the left-side toolbar. Useful when you want maximum
horizontal space for the editor and preview.

When the custom titlebar is enabled (Settings → UI → Custom Window
Titlebar), the toolbar can also be toggled from the hamburger icon in
the titlebar itself.

title: Zoom
body:
# Zoom

Adjust the entire UI's zoom level:

- `Ctrl+=` — zoom in
- `Ctrl+-` — zoom out
- `Ctrl+0` — reset to 100%

For a coarser change, pick a UI Scale in **Settings → UI**.

title: Themes
body:
# Themes

NoteLiner ships with three themes:

- **Midnight** — deep, low-contrast dark theme.
- **Dark** — neutral dark theme.
- **Light** — bright theme for daytime use.

Switch from **Settings → UI → Theme**, or from the Command Palette
(*Set Theme: Midnight / Dark / Light*).

title: Keyboard Shortcuts
body:
# Keyboard Shortcuts

A complete, always-up-to-date shortcut reference lives in
**Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts**. The list is generated from the
command registry, so anything the app responds to is documented there.

Highlights:

- `Ctrl+K` — Command Palette
- `Ctrl+N` / `Ctrl+D` — new / delete file
- `Ctrl+Shift+D` — duplicate file
- `Ctrl+O` — open folder
- `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` — undo / redo in the active tab
- `Ctrl+W` / `Ctrl+Shift+W` — close tab / reopen closed tab
- `Ctrl+P` — preview
- `Ctrl+E` / `Ctrl+Shift+E` — toggle sidebar / toolbar
- `Ctrl+F` / `Ctrl+Shift+F` — project search / find in file
- `Ctrl+,` — settings
- `F2` — rename the selected note or folder
- `Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+I` — bold / italic (in editor)
- `Ctrl+Shift+I` — about
